summary: Lookout listed as 'moody' in Troup County on the tnlandforms.us Georgia tower list; no source found on its history, condition or access.

evidence.supports: tnlandforms list: 'moody', Troup County, code gfc-417, coordinates 33.09999, -85.08370 (the row also has an elevation figure, 821, with no unit stated; not used)
The tnlandforms list was revised on 22 March 2016
GFC began phasing out tower operators in the late 1980s for an air patrol system; many towers were scrapped and sold
evidence.quote: In the late 1980s, the Georgia Forestry Commission began phasing out the tower operators in favor of an air patrol system. Many were scrapped and sold

evidence.supports: The same Vanishing Georgia post says Georgia's towers are at risk
evidence.quote: Though you may see them from time to time, Georgia's iconic fire towers are actually quite endangered

notes_for_editor: Very thin sources. The only source naming this tower is the tnlandforms list (cite 1), which gives the name in lower case as 'moody', county, elevation and code. No Georgia directory entry was found for it, and the web search turned up no history. Name variants excluded: Moody Tower in Ebro, Washington County, Florida (dismantled 2021, per a cached Washington County News item at data/raw/web/8e3cc3bb4d7c35230e3724ec39bd3f6a4b22bc31.bin), and Moody Air Force Base in Lowndes County, Georgia. Neither is this tower. The record's name 'moody' matches the tnlandforms list, so no correction is proposed. Agency is not stated by any source read, so no agency fact is recorded. Status, access and any build date need a human check, for example a GFC Troup County unit enquiry or recent imagery at 33.09999,-85.08370. Story is about 96 words, under the 120-word floor, because the sources hold little more. Verification 2026-10-21: the elevation (821 ft, 250 m) was removed from the story because the list gives no unit; the phase-out and endangered sentences were reworded from the source's wording.
